title: Shelve the artifacts so no object stands behind a taller one
instruction: Move the blue vase, green figurine, yellow bowl, orange pot and purple bead box from the grey cart on the left onto the wooden shelf on the right, with taller objects behind shorter ones so none is hidden. Leave at least 2 cm between objects and keep each at least 2 cm back from the shelf's front edge, the edge nearest you.
context: Collections-storage guidance puts small objects in front of larger ones and leaves space between them and the shelf edge, so every object is seen at inventory and none is lifted over another, the usual way stored objects get knocked and broken. Done by: museum technicians and conservators, collections managers, registrars.
setup: Coordinates are from the point midway between the two arm bases: 'in front' is away from the arms, 'left' and 'right' are the robot's. A dark grey cart tray (5 mm plastic floor, 5 mm walls 3 cm tall) is fixed in front of the left arm, its inside 14 to 40 cm in front of the arm bases and 17 to 45 cm left of centre. In it stand five solid painted-resin artifacts, upright: a blue vase (cylinder 6 cm across, 12 cm tall, 300 g) at 20 cm in front, 25 cm left; a green figurine (box 5 x 5 cm, 10 cm tall, 250 g, sides square to the table edges) at 31 cm in front, 25 cm left; a yellow bowl (closed cylinder 7 cm across, 6 cm tall, 200 g) at 18.5 cm in front, 37 cm left; an orange pot (cylinder 5 cm across, 5 cm tall, 150 g) at 28 cm in front, 37 cm left; a purple bead box (4 cm cube, 80 g, sides square) at 36 cm in front, 37 cm left (positions are centres). A brown wooden shelf board (2 cm thick, 26 cm wide, 24 cm deep) is fixed in front of the right arm, its front edge 20 cm in front of the arm bases, spanning 17 to 43 cm right of centre; a wooden lip 2 cm thick and 2 cm tall runs along its back edge, leaving a usable top 22 cm deep. A black rubber transfer pad (12 x 12 cm, 5 mm thick) is fixed on the centre line, its centre 22 cm in front of the arm bases. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: An artifact is shelved when it stands upright (axis tilted at most 15 degrees), has been set down with its bottom within 3 mm of the shelf top (not on another artifact, not held above it), and its whole footprint is on the usable top, between the front edge, the lip and the two side ends. Each shelved artifact whose footprint is at least 2 cm behind the front edge earns 0.2; one shelved nearer the edge earns 0.1. Each pair of shelved artifacts less than 2 cm apart (the gap between their outlines, each squared to the shelf edges) costs 0.05, with the total floored at 0. The score is 0 overall if any artifact on the shelf is hidden: another artifact on the shelf that is taller by 5 mm or more (standing heights: vase 12, figurine 10, bowl 6, pot 5, bead box 4 cm, so any taller one) has its back face (the side of its footprint farthest from the front edge) nearer the front edge than the hidden artifact's centre, so more than half of the hidden one stands behind it, and their centres are less than half their two widths plus 2 cm apart along the edge (widths: vase 6, figurine 5, bowl 7, pot 5, bead box 4 cm). For example, a pot centred 2 cm along the edge from the bead box (less than 5/2 + 4/2 + 2 = 6.5 cm) and 7 cm nearer the front has its back face 4.5 cm in front of the bead box's centre and hides it; 8 cm apart along the edge, they are in different lanes. Two artifacts side by side in a row, staggered so the taller one's back face is behind the shorter one's centre (the bowl 1.3 cm further forward than the pot puts the bowl's back face 2.2 cm behind the pot's centre), do not hide each other. An artifact is on the shelf, for hiding, when its centre is over the usable top and it has been set down: its bottom within 3 mm of the shelf top (standing or lying), or within 3 mm of the top of another artifact on the shelf with its centre over that artifact's footprint (stacked). One still held higher above the shelf hides nothing. A toppled artifact earns nothing but still hides others at its standing height; artifacts left in the cart, on the pad, on the table or the floor earn nothing. All five shelved, set back, spaced and none hidden: 1.0. The trial ends with success once all five meet this and stay still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) for 2.5 s; otherwise the score at the last step counts.
reset_notes: Stand the five artifacts upright back at their marks in the cart (tape outlines on the tray floor make this quick), the figurine and bead box with their sides square to the table edges. The shelf, cart and pad stay fixed; nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Approximate: the artifacts are solid rigid cylinders and boxes (the bowl is closed, the vase solid), so nothing chips or breaks; a hidden artifact stands in for one missed at inventory. The shelf is a board fixed on the table rather than a shelf in a rack. Every object has the same rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), grippier than glazed ceramic or wood.
